page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.large is an x86_64 virtualization instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, provisioned as 1 physical core yielding 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory capacity is set to 16.0 GB, providing an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets, alongside AES encryption acceleration. The server lacks attached local storage, relying on external network storage solutions, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes show that while single-threaded tasks perform at moderate industry levels, aggregate multi-threaded and memory throughput remain heavily constrained by the dual-vCPU ceiling. Single-core evaluation via Geekbench registers at 1242.0 and stress-ng achieves 1427.19, both aligning with the middle 50% tier. Conversely, multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core (1487.0) and overall PassMark CPU score (2341.78), fall into the bottom 10%. Memory read bandwidth reaches 13.43 GB/sec on large blocks and 106.04 GB/sec on cached blocks, positioning memory subsystems in the lower quartile.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.hfr6.large lies in its high memory density paired with entry-level multi-core compute capacity. Because of the generous 16.0 GB RAM allocation relative to its 2 vCPUs, it functions as a cost-efficient platform for memory-dependent applications that do not demand extensive parallel compute. Workload fit includes low-concurrency in-memory caching, lightweight relational database hosting, background data parsing, and modest application servers requiring generous memory footprints without heavy compute contention.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.large is a memory-rich virtual instance within the High Clock Speed family, running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 3.1 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark measurements reflect competent single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core at 1242.0 and stress-ng at 1427.19. However, total compute throughput is naturally limited by the low core count, resulting in lower-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth figures. The instance is suited for memory-oriented tasks with moderate CPU needs, such as small in-memory caches, lightweight database services, and basic enterprise web applications.
